text: {lead} taps out a steady beat beside the hill and the earth begins to wriggle. Turned up with the worms: Field Mushrooms.
A cheese wheel stuck in a hollow, as they do. {lead} gives it a shove and down the slope it goes, and the hollow gives up Typewriter Key.
A molehill, freshly heaped. {lead} drums a gentle rhythm on the ground and the worms come up to see what the fuss is. Among the soil: Field Mushrooms.
A cheese wheel stuck in a hollow, as they do. {lead} gives it a shove and down the slope it goes, and the hollow gives up a few coins.
The old trunk is hollow and ready to go. {lead} heaves, it topples, and out of the hollow rolls Field Mushrooms.
{lead} skims a stone over the pool and a bottle on a post tips over. Hanging from it: Drake's Drum.
A dead tree, waiting for an excuse. {lead} supplies one. In the roots, undisturbed for years: a few coins.
A coracle, left on the bank, light as a basket. {lead} gets in and paddles across without spinning more than twice. On the far side: Peregrine Feather.
The wheel has been here since last spring's chase. {lead} sets it rolling, and underneath is some loose change and a gratitude card.
{lead} circles the flock like it has done this all its life. The gate is clear in a minute. Someone has hung Cream Tea on the post.
A dead trunk, leaning on nothing much. {lead} puts its shoulder to it and over it goes with a crack. Underneath: a few coins.
{lead} tips the wheel over the lip and it bounds off downhill with great purpose. Where it was sitting: Cooper's Hill Ribbon.
A bale and a bend, and a bowl that wants lofting. {lead} swings and sends it up over the hedge in one long arc. It lands by Cream Tea.
A molehill, freshly heaped. {lead} drums a gentle rhythm on the ground and the worms come up to see what the fuss is. Among the soil: Claddagh Ring.
The bog water is dark and cold. {lead} ploughs through it with its face down and surfaces holding Bog Myrtle Sprig.
A peat pool, black as tea. {lead} dives in, flippers going, and comes up spluttering and delighted with Cup Tie Programme.
{lead} peers into the water, then pulls out, with great ceremony, Perch.
The wheel has been here since last spring's chase. {lead} sets it rolling, and underneath is some loose change and a gratitude card.
A flat stone and a still stretch of water. {lead} sends it dancing across, once, twice, five times, and something on the far side wobbles loose: Oak Acorn.
{lead} lofts the bowl clear over the hedge and the bale makes a fine step. You scramble over after it, picking out the odd twig.
You go back over the bale, and {lead} lofts the bowl after you. A passing cyclist nods, as if this is normal.
{lead} taps out a steady beat beside the hill and the earth begins to wriggle. Turned up with the worms: Silver Quaich.
{lead} shoves the dead trunk over the gap, where it lands with a satisfying thump. You walk across, arms out like a tightrope act.
You cross back over the trunk, arms out. {lead} goes under the stream bank, which is its own business.
The old trunk is hollow and ready to go. {lead} heaves, it topples, and out of the hollow rolls a few coins.
{lead} paddles you across in the little round boat, spinning once for good manners. The far bank is quiet, reedy and yours.
{lead} paddles you back. The boat drifts in a gentle circle the whole way, and nobody mentions it.
